content: Calea zacatechichi, also referred to as Dream Herb, Cheech, or Bitter Grass, is a plant traditionally utilized by the indigenous Chontal people of Oaxaca, Mexico, for the practice of oneiromancy, a form of divination based on dreams. Scientific studies have demonstrated that extracts from this plant can enhance reaction times and increase the frequency and/or recollection of dreams when compared to placebo and diazepam. The Chontal people also employ this plant as a medicinal herb to address gastrointestinal disorders. It is used as an appetite stimulant, a cathartic agent, a remedy for dysentery, and as an antipyretic to reduce fever. Chontal medicine men, who claim that the plant has the ability to clarify the senses, refer to it as thle-pela-kano, which translates to leaf of God. When seeking to determine the cause of an illness or the location of a distant or missing person, they use the dried leaves of the plant in various ways: smoking them, preparing infusions to drink, or placing them under a pillow before sleep. It is reported that the answers to their questions are revealed in dreams. To prepare the plant for use, dried leaves are crushed and steeped in hot water to make a tea, which is consumed slowly. Afterward, the user lies down in a quiet environment and smokes a cigarette made from the dried leaves of the same plant. For divinatory purposes, the Chontal people report that a typical dose consists of a handful of the dried plant. The user knows they have consumed an adequate dose when they experience a sense of tranquility and drowsiness, accompanied by the perception of their own heartbeat and pulse. The plant has a notably bitter taste, leading many users to prefer smoking it over drinking the tea. Cultivating Calea zacatechichi from seeds is challenging, and propagation is more commonly achieved through cuttings. The plant thrives in full sunlight, well-drained soils, and requires substantial irrigation. A recommended soil mixture for cultivation includes one-third rich substrate, one-third vermiculite, and one-third humus. If attempting to grow the plant from seeds, the seeds should be sown in the specified soil mix without being covered, moistened with water, and enclosed in a plastic bag to create a greenhouse effect. The seeds require 4 to 6 hours of light daily to germinate, and they must not dry out during this period, as this will prevent germination. In terms of legal status, Calea zacatechichi is an unscheduled substance in the United States, meaning it is legal to grow and sell. However, Louisiana State Act 159 prohibits the cultivation, harvesting, or sale of the plant within the state if it is intended for ingestion. This law applies to over 40 types of plants. In Tennessee, a proposed bill sought to make many hallucinogenic plants, including Calea zacatechichi, illegal when intended for human consumption, but the legislation was ultimately revised to only ban Salvia divinorum.
